risks.risk: Dependence on any single industry, customer segment or revenue stream, which the diversified multi-vertical model is explicitly built to offset
risks.note: MD&A section 6.1 states that presence across multiple service verticals 'helps reduce dependence on any single industry, customer segment, or revenue stream' and lets the Company balance market fluctuations in one segment with opportunities in others. Stated as a mitigation, it names the underlying exposure: earnings sit on a narrow set of verticals (Printing, Communication & Media, Record Management, Logistics & Cargo, Premium Mobility) and Printing Services is by far the largest of them, so a downturn in that one vertical is not offset by the smaller ones.

risks.risk: Client concentration in government institutions and BFSI enterprises, where relationships are contract/tender-based and retention is the stated defence
risks.note: MD&A section 6.2 names the customer base as 'government institutions, BFSI clients, corporates, and other enterprise customers' and positions long-term relationships, service quality and customised solutions as the means to enhance 'customer retention'. Institutional and BFSI mandates are periodically re-tendered and price-competed; loss or non-renewal of a large institutional account is the single largest revenue event the Company describes itself as managing.

risks.risk: Information-security and data-integrity risk from custody of third-party documents, records and communications
risks.note: MD&A section 6.3 places technology 'central to DJML's operations across document management, logistics, and business services' and commits continuing investment in 'digital platforms, information security measures, process automation, and employee awareness programmes to protect data'. The Corporate Overview repeats it as a core ESG/governance pillar ('robust data security frameworks', 'secure handling, transmission, and storage of critical information'). The Company physically and digitally holds client records for BFSI and government customers, so a breach is a client-loss and liability event, not just an IT incident.

risks.risk: Execution and capital-deployment risk on expansion, managed only by phasing rather than by committed contracts
risks.note: MD&A section 6.4 says investments are 'evaluated through phased implementation and ongoing performance monitoring to ensure operational efficiency and effective utilisation of resources'. Phasing is a control on how fast capital is committed, not proof of demand behind it; utilisation shortfalls on new capacity would show first in margin, and FY26 EBITDA margin already moved down while revenue grew sharply.

risks.risk: Structural displacement of the physical-print and paper-based record verticals by the digitisation the Company itself sells
risks.note: The Corporate Overview describes 'a shift from physical to digital ecosystems' through 'advanced digitization and document management solutions', and the ESG section lists 'paper reduction through digitization' as a key focus area in what it calls 'a resource-intensive industry'. The same trend that drives the Digitisation vertical erodes the Printing Solutions and physical Record Management volumes that currently carry the largest share of revenue; the transition has to be net-accretive, and the AR does not quantify the crossover.

risks.risk: Regulation-driven demand: Record Management volumes rest on compliance and information-governance mandates rather than on customer discretionary spend
risks.note: The MD&A segment outlook table attributes Records Management to 'continued demand driven by compliance and information governance requirements' and Digitisation to 'digital transformation initiatives across sectors'. Demand created by a retention/compliance rule is durable while the rule stands but is exposed to a change in statutory retention periods or a regulator permitting digital-only custody, which would compress the physical storage business.

risks.risk: Logistics & Cargo was the only vertical to contract in FY26, while segment outlook ties it to external infrastructure and trade expansion
risks.note: In the MD&A segment-wise revenue disclosure, Logistics & Cargo Services was the sole vertical whose revenue fell year-on-year; every other vertical grew. Its stated outlook depends on 'infrastructure and trade expansion' - drivers outside the Company's control - so recovery in this vertical is not management-determined.

risks.risk: Dependence on the single material subsidiary Sai Links for the entire Premium Mobility vertical
risks.note: The Board's report records that 'as on March 31, 2026, the Company had a subsidiary, namely Sai Links' and that a Policy for Determining Material Subsidiaries is in place; the segment disclosure shows Premium Mobility Services is carried entirely by Sailinks and is the second-largest vertical after Printing. Consolidated revenue therefore depends materially on one subsidiary whose vertical grew only marginally in FY26, and any governance, licensing or fleet issue there flows straight to consolidated results.

hero.oneLiner: An integrated communication, printing, logistics, record-management and technology-enabled business-services platform for Indian corporates, BFSI, government and healthcare clients, with an international presence in China.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: An integrated communication, printing, logistics, record-management and technology-enabled business-services platform for Indian corporates, BFSI, government and healthcare clients, with an international presence in China.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: DJ Mediaprint & Logistics Limited operates as an integrated enterprise combining communication, printing, logistics, data management and technology into a unified platform, spanning core verticals of Printing (including security printing), Mailing Services, Logistics, Scanning & Digitization, Record Management Solutions and Newspaper Advertisement Services. Its client base includes banks, insurers, government bodies and healthcare institutions across India, and it has extended into premium mobility through its subsidiary Sailinks and into global/cross-border logistics via its Guangzhou, China presence.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- Sai Links (Sailinks) — subsidiary: 51% stake acquired (2022), extending DJML into premium mobility solutions
- D.J. Corporation — related party: Wholly owned by the Company's directors (100% directors' stake); counterparty for sales/purchase transactions
- Dynamic Superways & Exports Ltd. — related party: Entity with common directors

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Printing:** Security printing (IBA-approved license), Print-to-Post services
- **Mailing Services:** Bulk Mailing, Speed Post services
- **Logistics:** Domestic logistics & cargo solutions, Global & Cross-Border Logistics Solutions
- **Scanning & Digitization:** Bulk scanning, Document digitisation
- **Record Management Solutions:** Record storage and management centres
- **Newspaper Advertisement Services:** Newspaper advertisement placement
- **Premium Mobility:** Sailinks premium mobility services (51% subsidiary)

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- India (pan-India presence across 18+ locations)
- Guangzhou, China (international presence)
- BFSI institutions, banks and insurers
- Government & regulatory bodies
- Healthcare institutions
- Corporate clients

certifications.title: Certs (RHP)
certifications.body:
- ISO certifications (achieved 2018)
- IBA-approved security printing license (2019)

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's GDP projected to grow at approximately 7% annually, positioning it as a USD 7 trillion economy by 2030, supporting demand for DJML's integrated services
- Digitisation of government and private-sector records viewed as a multi-year, multi-thousand-crore opportunity
- National Logistics Policy and PM Gati Shakti driving formalisation and demand for organised, technology-enabled logistics operators
- Digital communication channels (Email, SMS, WhatsApp) becoming regulatory requirements in BFSI, supporting demand for communication services
- India's logistics market projected to grow from ~USD 240-246 billion (2025) to ~USD 357-362 billion by 2030 (8-11% CAGR)
- Cross-border e-commerce logistics in India projected to grow at CAGRs exceeding 20-29% through 2030
- Global records/electronic records management market (~USD 10-11 billion in 2025-26) expected to grow at ~11% CAGR through the early 2030s on compliance and digital-archiving needs
- Global document management system market forecast to reach ~USD 18 billion by 2030, with the IDP segment expanding at over 25% CAGR
- India's commercial printing market (~USD 54 billion in 2025) expected to grow at a steady ~3% CAGR to ~USD 72 billion by 2035, supported by regulatory and enterprise documentation needs
- India's DOOH advertising market projected to grow at 10-14% CAGR through 2030
- India's business travel/premium mobility market projected to grow from ~USD 45 billion (2025) to ~USD 82 billion by 2034 (7-9% CAGR)

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Formal entry into Global & Cross-Border Logistics Solutions during FY26, extending the domestic communication/logistics platform to serve international trade via the Guangzhou, China presence
- Continue integrating communication, printing, logistics, record management, digitisation and mobility (via Sailinks) into a single unified service platform
- Strengthen digital capabilities across document management, communication platforms and integrated business solutions
- Maintain disciplined capital allocation and a balanced capital structure to fund infrastructure expansion
- Expand Record Management footprint with new centres and consolidate management oversight through the new Administrative Office in Belapur, Navi Mumbai
- The Board recommended a final dividend for FY26. Management's stated capital-allocation philosophy emphasises disciplined capital management, a balanced capital structure, and reinvestment of retained earnings into infrastructure expansion (Record Management Centres, the new Administrative Office in Belapur, and integration of Sailinks) to fund future growth while maintaining a prudent, conservative leverage position.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: DJML's footprint has grown through a series of named projects: a corporate office and manufacturing facility set up in Navi Mumbai (2016); Record Management Centres added in Bhiwandi (2021), Bhiwandi & Mysuru (2022), Puducherry (2025), and Bhiwandi & Delhi (FY26); an advanced logistics fleet and digital printing capability upgrade together with establishment of an international presence in Guangzhou, China (2024); the FY26 formal entry into Global & Cross-Border Logistics Solutions leveraging that Guangzhou presence; and a new Administrative Office established in Belapur, Navi Mumbai (FY26) to consolidate management oversight. The Company's 51% acquisition of Sailinks (2022) extended the platform into premium mobility solutions.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Integrated end-to-end service platform spanning communication, printing, logistics, data management and technology, enabling cross-selling and single-point client accountability
- Long-standing institutional relationships, including LIC onboarded as the Company's first major client in 1999
- Diversified revenue base across multiple service verticals (printing, mailing, logistics, digitisation, record management, advertisement, mobility) reducing dependence on any single segment or customer
- International presence in Guangzhou, China supporting cross-border sourcing and coordination
- Established external credibility via a CRISIL rating (2011) and an IBA-approved security printing license (2019)
